observed_claims: The Link response header supplies URLs for additional result pages.
Clients may use the supplied next URL directly.
per_page is automatically carried into Link URLs when supported.

finding.statement: Raw-string equality for GitHub pagination continuation URLs is stricter than the documented continuation contract and can reject semantically equivalent URLs when query parameters are reordered.
finding.uncertainty: GitHub documentation defines Link URLs as usable continuations but does not promise stable query-parameter ordering.
finding.non_duplication: Prior work validated exact raw URLs, Link chaining, API version confirmation, request IDs, record IDs, and body digests. This slice addresses semantic URL equivalence while retaining fail-closed endpoint and filter constraints.

artifact.design: Parse the URL structurally; accept query-order differences only; require HTTPS api.github.com, exact repository workflow-runs path, exactly one head_sha/per_page/page parameter, exact commit, page, and page size; reject extras, duplicates, userinfo, fragments, origin drift, and path drift.

falsification_route: Capture an authenticated GitHub workflow-runs Link header for an exact commit and test every next URL against the validator.
Falsify the design if GitHub emits a required continuation parameter outside head_sha, per_page, and page for this endpoint.
Falsify the implementation if two URLs with different endpoint semantics both canonicalize as verified.
limits: No authenticated live Link header was captured in this run.
The artifact is not yet integrated into validate-workflow-page-chain.mjs.
Passing unit tests do not prove GitHub provider behavior.
